newsitem.title: USA: O.J. Simpson cites new evidence, wants new trial.
newsitem.headline: O.J. Simpson cites new evidence, wants new trial.

text.p: O.J. Simpson, acquitted of murder but found liable in a civil trial for the deaths of his ex-wife and her friend, wants a new trial, according to court documents filed on Tuesday.
In motions filed with the Los Angeles County Superior Court, his lawyers argued Simpson did not get a fair trial when he was sued by the victims' families.
It also called the total $33.5 million damages the civil trial jury awarded the plaintiffs "excessive," and asked Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki to reduce the amount.

One of the motions set out 12 legal grounds for overturning the verdict. One reason for granting a new trial was "newly discovered evidence, material for the defendant" which could not have been presented at the civil trial.
It gave no details of the "new evidence", nor did it specify the "irregularity in proceedings" or "misconduct of the jury" that it also cited.
There were also "errors in law" that "materially affected the substantial rights of the defendant and prevented him from obtaining a fair trial," the motion said.
Tuesday was the deadline for Simpson's defence lawyers to file an appeal or any other motions relating to the civil trial, which ended last month with the damages award.
The jury in Santa Monica found Simpson responsible for the deaths of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman, who were found slashed to death in June 1994.
In the culmination of three months of testimony in the wrongful-death case, the jury slapped Simpson with $8.5 million in compensatory damages and a total of $25 million in punitive damages.
Fujisaki signed judgments on March 10 ordering Simpson to pay Goldman's father Fred $13.475 million, Goldman's mother Sharon Rufo $7.525 million and the estate of Nicole Brown Simpson $12.5 million.
"The damages awarded by the jury were excessive both as to compensatory and punitive damages," the defence motion said. "The evidence was insufficient to justify the verdicts."

Simpson, a former NFL player, TV personality and actor, had been acquitted of the murders by a criminal court jury in October 1995, but the civil suit for wrongful death was brought against him by the families of the victims.
The motions were filed by one of Simpson's civil trial legal team, Daniel Leonard. There was no immediate comment from the plaintiffs' lawyers.
